name: One in-character line (second punchline)
template: A single sentence the character would say, that only makes sense after watching
examples: Can I stay with you all day
mechanism: The caption is read after the Reel; a second punchline earns a like or a send on the way out. No hashtags, no summary, no CTA.
anti_pattern: Describing what happens in the video; asking for follows.
observed: Every 1M+ skit Reel sampled used this or no caption

name: Two words or nothing
mechanism: For visual-first Reels the caption has no job; leaving it near-empty keeps the frame clean and lets the audio/visual carry it.
anti_pattern: Hashtag blocks; a paragraph under a 9-second visual.
observed: 48M Reel captioned 'Going up⬆️'; a 163K skit posted with no caption

name: The line that expands the hook
template: One sentence that adds the detail the video deliberately left out (the number, the name, the exception), then stop
examples: It's the second thing on the list, not the first. Save this for packing week.
Works for RDLs too — but only if you stop before lockout.
mechanism: Gives a reason to read (and save) without repeating the video; a soft 'save this' embedded in a useful sentence is not engagement bait.
anti_pattern: 'SAVE THIS!!' as a standalone CTA; 20 hashtags.
observed: Practitioner pattern; the sampled skit accounts don't need it

name: A question the video answers badly on purpose
template: "<Two options>?" where the video clearly picks the wrong one
examples: Text back in 2 minutes or 2 days?
mechanism: Disagreement is the comment driver; a binary choice makes commenting effortless and keeps replies civil enough to stay.
anti_pattern: 'Comment YES if you agree' — that is bait and gets deprioritized.
observed: Used as a pinned comment on a 1.9M Reel; 14 replies on the pin, 40+ on the seeded thread
